You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

This task's transformation rule isn't clear from the test input alone — the pattern of 2s across the three-row bands could follow several rules (shifting, overlaying, extracting shapes). A single demonstration will let me infer the rule reliably rather than guess and risk wrong submissions.

{"action": "request_demos"}

My interpretation of the fill rule was wrong somewhere — possibly the fill direction or which cells change. Since the demo rows only showed 2s as a contiguous prefix (with the fill running to the right edge), the interleaved 2/3 rows in the test are ambiguous. One more demo should clarify.

{"action": "request_demos"}

The demos only show a pattern run starting at the left edge, so they don't disambiguate how the fill interacts with rows where 2s are scattered. Rather than burn more attempts guessing, I'll get another demo to pin down the exact fill extent.

{"action": "request_demos"}

Demo 3 confirms fill to the right edge, but since both my "first-to-end" and "last-to-end" variants failed, the remaining natural variant is: fill only cells *between* the first and last pattern cell (which in demos reaches the right edge because the pattern is a prefix there... actually no). Reconsidering: in demo 1, row 17's last 0 is at column 5, and output fills columns 6–10, i.e., after the last pattern cell too. So demos fill to the edge regardless. Given the failures, the alternative is filling the *first* segment only: from the start of the row up to (but not including) the first pattern cell, background becomes 1 — matching demo 1's row 2 if... no.

The one variant consistent with all three demos yet untried: fill from the first pattern cell to the end (attempt 2) failed, so perhaps pattern cells *change too* — the 2s in pattern rows also become 1, leaving only the leading background. For demo 1, that yields 8→? No, row 2 output keeps 8s.

I'll try: in each pattern row, background cells to the right of the *first* pattern cell become 1, and pattern cells remain — but with fill also applied to rows *between* pattern rows in a band? No. Given attempts remain, submit the between-first-and-last variant.
